messages:
Mira: quick report — ran into a weird stale-prefetch case while testing compaction pacing. leaving notes here before I file a short postmortem.
Jose: curious, what was the scenario? compaction + handoff?
Mira: not a handoff. repro: prefix was prefetched into node-A, then compaction on node-A ran and reclaimed an old segment id that the prefetched header still referenced. later a read used the prefetched header -> decoder tried to fetch segment X -> 404 from local store -> we fell back to stale on remote node which still had an old copy. end result: served older value during a concurrent write+compact window.
Fatima: hmm that's subtle. can you paste the minimal log snip?
Mira: sure: \n```
[10:12:01] PREFETCH tenant=ten-9 prefix=ord-43 gen=17 node=node-A header->seg=892
[10:12:10] COMPACT tenant=ten-9 node=node-A removed_seg=892 new_gen=18
[10:12:11] WRITE tenant=ten-9 prefix=ord-43 value=v2 epoch=203
[10:12:12] READ hit cache header->seg=892 decode->fetch seg 892 -> 404 local, remote fallback -> returned v1 (stale)
```
Lee: so compaction increments a local generation and reclaims segments; cached header still points to reclaimed seg id. we end up with a split brain between local compacted state and remote nodes/replicas.
Nina: two obvious fixes: 1) on compaction bump a prefix.gen and broadcast; cached entries must carry gen and be rejected if gen < current. 2) make compaction GC lazy: keep seg ids around until all caches ack or TTL expires. both tradeoffs.
Jose: gen-bump seems straightforward: prefetched headers carry gen, compare on hit, fallback on mismatch. but broadcast reliability is a concern when compaction runs frequently on high-churn tenants.
Fatima: agreed. if tenants with aggressive compaction cause gen churn, we'll pay validation overhead. maybe we only validate when the header references a segment that fails to fetch (404) instead of validating every hit. cheaper on the common path.
Mira: the bug here is that 404 is a signal we treat as "missing segment -> try remote" and then remote had stale copy. if we reject cache earlier via gen mismatch we force canonical read and avoid remote fallback.
Lee: another hybrid: keep a lightweight per-tenant compaction_epoch that increments on compaction; nodes cache compaction_epoch for tenants and only validate cached entries if cached.gen < cached_compaction_epoch. We can TTL the cached epoch entry so most reads are local compares.
Nina: key operational questions: 1) how frequently do compactions happen per tenant in prod? 2) how many prefetched objects reference reclaimed seg ids? we need metrics first.
Jose: I can add metrics: compact.events.total, compact.per_tenant.rate, prefetched_header_refs.count (by seg_status: present|reclaimed|missing). also add prefetched_rejects_on_gen_mismatch.count.
Fatima: suggested experiment path: \n- instrument a staging cluster with a synthetic compaction-heavy tenant (fast writes + compaction cadence)\n- implement option A: gen-bump + local compare (cheap compare path) + fallback to store on mismatch\n- implement option B: lazy GC: mark reclaimed but keep seg content pinned for Xs until caches TTL out\n- sampling: enable gen-compare sampling at 5% initially to measure regressions
Lee: performance notes: gen-compare is just an integer compare; overhead is minimal if we cache tenant.compaction_epoch locally. broadcast cost only on compaction events. lazy GC pins storage and increases disk pressure. both have ops consequences.
Mira: security/consistency nit: ensure when we fallback to canonical store we get strong read-after-write semantics for the write that triggered compaction. the canonical path must prune/resolve seg-level indirections correctly.
Nina: rollout plan: canary on a single shard, 1 tenant, run for 24h. measure prefetched_rejects, latency p99 and segment-404 rate.
Jose: Ill add the metrics and a feature flag to toggle gen-compare. Fatima, can you sketch the gen broadcast proto? should be tiny: (tenant, new_gen, origin_node, ts).
Fatima: yep, small TTLed k-v entry in our gossip channel + write-ahead to sequencer for durability if we want stronger guarantees. sequencer write means extra RPCs though.
Lee: durability tradeoff: best-effort broadcast is probably enough if we also handle the 404->fallback path correctly. then gen is a fast local check and 404 still triggers canonical fetch as a safety net.
Mira: I'll build a repro harness that runs tight write+compact cycles and measures stale hits. planning to run Friday in staging.
infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled: kv-prefetch-gen-check -> shard-canary-3 at 2024-07-02T02:00:00Z by @Mira.
Mira: next actions: Jose wires metrics + flag, Fatima drafts broadcast proto & small TTLed cache design, Lee documents op/space tradeoffs, Nina coordinates canary window. will post results and recommended default (likely gen-compare with 30s compaction aggregation). :rocket:
